items.followUp: State two causes of deforestation and describe two effects it can have on biodiversity.

rubric.why: Clearing forests for agricultural land is a cause of deforestation.
rubric.description: Identifies clearing forests for agriculture or cultivation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid agricultural cause.

rubric.why: Demand for wood and land for human development also contributes to deforestation.
rubric.description: Identifies one further valid cause, such as timber or fuelwood collection, urbanization, population growth or industrial development.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one additional valid cause.

rubric.why: Forest clearing removes the habitats organisms depend on.
rubric.description: States that deforestation causes habitat loss or habitat destruction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying habitat loss or destruction.

rubric.why: Organisms may decline or become extinct when their habitats and resources are lost.
rubric.description: States that species may decline or become extinct.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying decline or extinction of species.

rubric.why: Deforestation reduces biological variety and can disrupt relationships within ecosystems.
rubric.description: States that biodiversity decreases or that food chains or ecosystem relationships are disrupted.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a further effect on biodiversity or ecosystem relationships.

modelAnswer: Deforestation is caused by clearing forests for agriculture and cultivation.
Other causes include cutting trees for timber or fuelwood, urbanization, population growth and industrial development.
Deforestation causes habitat loss and habitat destruction.
Species may decline or become extinct.
Biodiversity decreases, and food chains and ecosystem relationships may be disrupted.
